name: garrow
author: food and the kitchen (kitchen agent)
description:
garrow v2 (direction: food and the kitchen) - A TRAY PIZZA, CUT INTO SLICES. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = seven lines. Line 1 is "x k y j": two topping letters each followed by one digit 1-3, e.g. "m2o1". The remaining lines are the uncut pizza: a crust row of "#", four dough rows "#...mm....oo...#" (cheese is ".", every topping is a 2-cell piece of a repeated lowercase letter, no two pieces touch), and a closing crust row. Rows are 28-34 characters wide including the crust, four topping letters drawn from "mpotacsb", 4-5 pieces per row (v1: 30-38 wide, 5-6 per row, digits up to 6).

ANSWER = the same picture with the knife lines drawn in: a "|" inserted straight down through every row at the same columns. Nothing else may change, so the player's only freedom is where the cuts go; the picture itself is given.

RULE (unchanged from v1, and the scorer is byte-identical to v1's). score = 1 iff (1) the answer, with every "|" deleted, is exactly the clue's dough rows (lines with no "." - crust rows, a header, blank lines - are ignored, so the picture is strict but the trimmings are free); (2) the cuts are at the same columns in every row; (3) there are 4-8 slices, each at least 3 characters wide, and every slice carries at least one topping ("nobody gets a plain slice"); and (4) for EACH of the two named toppings, the number of slices holding TWO OR MORE pieces of it equals its digit - where a piece the knife went through counts for the slice on BOTH sides of the cut. In the picture a halved topping is drawn as "m|m", so "this slice got two mushrooms, and one of them is the half" is readable by eye.

WHY V2 EXISTS. Ladder run lad-garrow-v1-1 (2 opus players, 6x0.5 s + 3 s final): finals 25 % and 6 %, mean 15 %, leaning too_hard; kid judge 3.2/5 with "object" scored 2. Neither player found the rule. Both read the digits as something about the knife cutting pieces - 1a "severed(L) = how many L-dominoes a cut passes through" (which scored 29 % in training, so it was a paying local optimum), 1b "slices where L outnumbers the other topping". Both are shadows of the real count. Both hard-coded 7 slices and widths 3-7 from two neat demos, and both said afterwards that the kid reading they had missed was "the pieces don't have to be the same size" and "why does THIS cut count?". So v2 changes nothing about the rule and everything about what the demo picture says out loud:
  (a) UNEVEN WIDTHS. solve() now draws its cutting uniformly from all compositions of the width into n parts of at least 3 (v1 sprinkled the surplus one column at a time, which piles up near-equal slices). Demo width spread is now 8.1 columns on average, 98 % of demos have a slice at least 5 columns wider than their thinnest, and all of 4,5,6,7,8 slices appear (4-8: 29/29/23/14/5 % of 600 demos). Neatness is visibly not the point.
  (b) SMALL DIGITS. Both digits are now 1-3 (measured over 600 clues: 389/435/376). "Two slices got two mushrooms" is a thing a kid can point at; "five slices got two mushrooms" is a thing a kid counts wrong.
  (c) THE HEADLINE PICTURE. Every demo is required to show, in at least one COUNTED slice, a halved piece sitting beside a whole piece of the same letter (grade() checks it; 94.5 % of demos are full grade-0 demos, 3.5 % fall back to a weaker one). The intended sentence - "that slice has two mushrooms, and one of them got cut in half" - is drawn in every demo rather than left to be inferred.
  (d) THE SEVERED SHADOW IS KILLED INSIDE ONE DEMO. In v1 the filter only forbade severed(L) == k, and severed happened to land on k-1 in four of 1a's five demos, which is exactly the trap that ate their run. v2 requires the two named toppings to have DIFFERENT severed-minus-digit offsets in every clue's witness and in every grade-0 demo, so no law of the form "severed = digit + c" survives even one demo.
  (e) EQUAL SLICES ARE NEVER AN ANSWER. generate() now rejects any (k,j) pair that some equal-width cutting (three roundings x 4-8 slices) achieves, so the pizza's famous operation is falsified by construction rather than by luck: 11.2 % -> 0.00 %.
  (f) A LESS BUSY TRAY: narrower, 4-5 pieces a row, named letters with 4-7 pieces, so the two toppings the clue names can be scanned by eye.

WHY THE CLUE STILL NAMES TWO TOPPINGS. The obvious further softening is one letter and one digit. Measured on v1 clues: a player who has the format and cuts at random satisfies ONE count 25.3 % of the time and BOTH counts 3.0 %. A single-count clue would therefore hand a player who never gets past "the answer is the picture with bars in it" a 25 % floor - as much as v1's better player scored with a whole (wrong) theory - and no witness table could stay clean. The second count is what keeps blind play near 3 %; it costs the kid nothing, because the two digits are two instances of the same sentence ("two slices got two mushrooms, one slice got two olives"), not a second rule. Kept, with both digits small.

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. (1) One demo shows the answer is the clue picture with bars inserted - kid-easy and worth nothing on its own. (2) The two letters name two toppings, so every demo carries two equations of the same law. (3) The counted quantity is small and drawn: the demo has a slice with two of the letter in it, one of them halved. (4) The last step is the halves convention, and it is still load-bearing: a player with the right measurement who counts a halved piece for the left slice only scores 22 %, for neither slice 15 %.

MEASURED WITNESS TABLE (600 fresh clues per version, identical harness; a strategy "builds" an answer by searching well-formed cuttings that satisfy its own law, then is scored by the real rule).
  strategy                                  v1        v2
  true rule (solve)                     100.0 %   100.0 %
  equal-width slices, best of 4-8 cuts   11.17 %    0.00 %
  severed = n                            22.83 %   11.33 %
  severed = n-1                          14.33 %    6.50 %
  L outnumbers the other topping          7.50 %    9.83 %
  random well-formed cutting, 4-8         2.17 %    3.50 %
  one constant answer for every clue      0.17 %    0.17 %
  demo replay (previous clue's answer)    0.00 %    0.00 %
A second blind sampler that draws widths the way solve() does (uniform compositions) scores 4.1 % on v2, so the floor is 3-4 %. The wrong-family theories are now worth 2-3x the floor instead of v1's 10x, and the nearly-right ones are worth more than they were: the payoff ladder is 3-4 % (no idea) -> 8-12 % (the knife family) -> 15-22 % (right measurement, wrong halves) -> 100 %.

RIVAL LAWS ON V2 (250 clues, "built" = fraction of clues for which the belief can be satisfied at all by a well-formed cutting, "scores" = what it is worth against the real scorer): slices with 2+ x, halves counting left only 44/22.4 %; halves counting nowhere 34/14.8 %; slices with any x 30/3.6 %; slices with 3+ x 10/0.8 %; 2+ of ANY one topping 26/0.0 %; x pieces the knife cut 96/11.6 %; other pieces cut 97/2.8 %; all pieces cut 33/1.2 %; number of slices 0/0.0 %; number of cuts 8/0.4 %; slices with no x 90/1.6 %; slices with 2+ toppings 6/0.4 %; x outnumbers the other named topping 92/7.6 %. Two readings remain near-synonyms of the truth rather than rivals - "slices with exactly two x" 90/52.8 % and "pairs of x sharing a slice" 78/51.2 % - but both already carry the halves convention, so a player who reaches them has the insight.

JUNK AND SHAPE ATTACKS (300 clues, scorer unchanged from v1 so these are confirmations): empty, whitespace, 4000 chars of junk, the clue itself, the uncut pizza, another clue's answer - all 0.00 %. On an otherwise correct answer: reference 100 %; trailing spaces, crust rows removed, blank lines inserted, an extra header line - all 100 % (robust about form); all cuts removed, one cut missing in one row, cuts shifted by one in one row, an extra cut at the edge, a row deleted, a row duplicated, upper-cased, dots turned to spaces, a topping moved, reversed left-right, rows reversed - all 0.00 %.

SPEED (this was a real defect in v1: the arena served only ~50 items per 0.5 s round on garrow versus 400-800 on other classes, and generate() was the whole of it - it sampled 420 cuttings per attempt and scored each one piece by piece). v2's generate() keeps prefix sums of piece columns, so one candidate cutting costs O(slices) instead of O(pieces), and it samples 48 of them per attempt: mean 0.54 ms, median 0.42 ms, p99 1.5 ms, max 11.6 ms over 3000 seeds (v1: mean 8.7 ms, median 7.8 ms, max 38 ms) - a 16x cut, and the clue is still deterministic per seed. solve(): mean 13 ms, median 1.6 ms, max 322 ms (v1: mean 86 ms, median 36 ms, max 337 ms); it samples cuttings, keeps the best-graded one, and widens its budget automatically when a clue's count pair is very rare. 3000 seeds: no empty clue, and score(clue, solve(clue)) == 1 on every one. Sizes: scorer 474 chars, solve 4997, clue <= 214 chars, solution <= 251.
generate:
def place(r, W, alpha, m):
    """m toppings along one row, every pair separated by at least one cheese cell."""
    slots = r.sample(range(W - 1 - 3 * (m - 1)), m)
    slots.sort()
    cells = ["."] * W
    pcs = []
    for i, j in enumerate(slots):
        j += 3 * i
        L = r.choice(alpha)
        cells[j] = L
        cells[j + 1] = L
        pcs.append((j + 1, L))
    return "#" + "".join(cells) + "#", pcs


def cutb(r, T, n):
    """A uniformly random cutting of a T-wide tray into n slices, each at least 3 wide."""
    b = []
    t = p = 0
    for x in sorted(r.sample(range(T - 2 * n - 1), n - 1)):
        t += x - p + 3
        p = x + 1
        b.append(t)
    return b


def sums(P, T, xy):
    """raw[c] = pieces of a letter with left cell in column c; pre[c] = how many lie left of c."""
    raw = [[0] * (T + 1) for _ in range(3)]
    for c, L in P:
        raw[2][c] += 1
        if L == xy[0]:
            raw[0][c] += 1
        elif L == xy[1]:
            raw[1][c] += 1
    pre = []
    for a in raw:
        q = [0] * (T + 2)
        t = 0
        for i in range(T + 1):
            q[i] = t
            t += a[i]
        pre.append(q)
    return raw, pre


def kof(b, T, pre):
    """(k, k) for the two named toppings, or None if some slice carries no topping at all."""
    p0, p1, pa = pre
    k0 = k1 = s = 0
    for x in b + [T]:
        lo = s - 1 if s else 0
        if pa[x] == pa[lo]:
            return None
        if p0[x] - p0[lo] > 1:
            k0 += 1
        if p1[x] - p1[lo] > 1:
            k1 += 1
        s = x
    return k0, k1


def counts(b, T, pre):
    """Per-slice counts of the two named toppings; None if some slice carries no topping."""
    A = ([], [])
    s = 0
    p0, p1, pa = pre
    for x in b + [T]:
        lo = s - 1 if s else 0
        if pa[x] == pa[lo]:
            return None
        A[0].append(p0[x] - p0[lo])
        A[1].append(p1[x] - p1[lo])
        s = x
    return A


def tell(b, A, raw, i):
    """(severed pieces, is a halved piece sitting beside a whole one) for named topping i."""
    sv = [0] * (len(b) + 1)
    tot = 0
    a = raw[i]
    for j, x in enumerate(b):
        q = a[x - 1]
        tot += q
        sv[j] += q
        sv[j + 1] += q
    return tot, any(A[i][s] > 1 and 0 < sv[s] < A[i][s] for s in range(len(sv)))


def eqb(T, n, m):
    """The three ways a tidy-minded player cuts a T-wide tray into n even slices."""
    if m == 2:
        return [(i * T + n // 2) // n for i in range(1, n)]
    q, e = T // n, T % n
    w = [q + (i < e if m else i >= n - e) for i in range(n)]
    b = []
    t = 0
    for v in w[:-1]:
        t += v
        b.append(t)
    return b


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    for _ in range(24):
        W = r.randint(26, 32)
        T = W + 2
        alpha = r.sample("mpotacsb", 4)
        rows = []
        P = []
        for _ in range(4):
            row, pcs = place(r, W, alpha, r.randint(4, 5))
            rows.append(row)
            P += pcs
        cnt = {}
        for c, L in P:
            cnt[L] = cnt.get(L, 0) + 1
        cand = [L for L in alpha if 4 <= cnt.get(L, 0) <= 7]
        if len(cand) < 2:
            continue
        xy = r.sample(cand, 2)
        raw, pre = sums(P, T, xy)
        hist = {}
        good = set()
        for _ in range(48):
            n = r.randint(4, 8)
            b = cutb(r, T, n)
            q = kof(b, T, pre)
            if q is None:
                continue
            k0, k1 = q
            hist[q] = hist.get(q, 0) + 1
            if 0 < k0 < 4 and 0 < k1 < 4 and q not in good:
                A = counts(b, T, pre)
                s0, h0 = tell(b, A, raw, 0)
                s1, h1 = tell(b, A, raw, 1)
                if (h0 or h1) and s0 - k0 != s1 - k1:
                    good.add(q)
        best = [q for q in good if 0 < hist[q] < 7]
        if not best:
            continue
        for n in range(4, 9):                      # equal slices must never be an answer
            for m in (0, 1, 2):
                q = kof(eqb(T, n, m), T, pre)
                if q in best:
                    best.remove(q)
        if not best:
            continue
        best.sort(key=lambda q: hist[q])
        q = best[0]
        crust = "#" * T
        return "%s%d%s%d\n%s\n%s\n%s" % (xy[0], q[0], xy[1], q[1], crust,
                                           "\n".join(rows), crust)
    return ""
solve:
def pcs(rows):
  P = []
  for i, row in enumerate(rows):
    j = 0
    while j < len(row) - 1:
      if row[j].isalpha() and row[j + 1] == row[j]:
        P.append((i, j, row[j]))
        j += 2
      else:
        j += 1
  return P

# Uniform over compositions of T into n parts >= 3: demo widths are uneven.
def cutb(r, T, n):
  b = []
  t = p = 0
  for x in sorted(r.sample(range(T - 2 * n - 1), n - 1)):
    t += x - p + 3
    p = x + 1
    b.append(t)
  return b

def sums(P, T, xy):
  raw = [[0] * (T + 1) for _ in range(3)]
  for _, c, L in P:
    raw[2][c] += 1
    if L == xy[0]:
      raw[0][c] += 1
    elif L == xy[1]:
      raw[1][c] += 1
  pre = []
  for a in raw:
    q = [0] * (T + 2)
    t = 0
    for i in range(T + 1):
      q[i] = t
      t += a[i]
    pre.append(q)
  return raw, pre

def cnt(b, T, pre):
  A = ([], [])
  s = 0
  for x in b + [T]:
    lo = s - 1 if s else 0
    if pre[2][x] == pre[2][lo]:
      return None
    A[0].append(pre[0][x] - pre[0][lo])
    A[1].append(pre[1][x] - pre[1][lo])
    s = x
  return A

def tell(b, A, raw, i):
  sv = [0] * (len(b) + 1)
  tot = 0
  for j, x in enumerate(b):
    q = raw[i][x - 1]
    tot += q
    sv[j] += q
    sv[j + 1] += q
  return tot, any(A[i][s] > 1 and 0 < sv[s] < A[i][s] for s in range(len(sv)))

# The true count for topping x plus every rival reading of the same cut picture.
def look(b, n, P, x, y, H):
  A = [0] * n
  Lf = [0] * n
  Wh = [0] * n
  Y = [0] * n
  pc = [0] * n
  rc = [[0] * n for _ in range(H)]
  lc = [{} for _ in range(n)]
  sx = so = 0
  for row, c, L in P:
    s1 = bisect.bisect_right(b, c)
    s2 = bisect.bisect_right(b, c + 1)
    st = s2 != s1
    for s in ((s1, s2) if st else (s1,)):
      pc[s] += 1
      lc[s][L] = lc[s].get(L, 0) + 1
      if L == x:
        A[s] += 1
        rc[row][s] += 1
      elif L == y:
        Y[s] += 1
    if L == x:
      Lf[s1] += 1
      if st:
        sx += 1
      else:
        Wh[s1] += 1
    elif st:
      so += 1
  g = lambda t: sum(1 for v in A if v >= t)
  return (g(2), sx, so, g(1) - g(2),
      (sum(1 for v in Lf if v > 1), sum(1 for v in Wh if v > 1), g(1), g(3),
      sum(1 for d in lc if any(t > 1 for t in d.values())),
      sum(1 for p in P if p[2] == x), sx, so, sx + so, n, n - 1,
      sum(v for v in A if v > 1), n - g(1),
      sum(1 for s in range(n) if any(rc[i][s] > 1 for i in range(H))),
      sum(1 for v in pc if v > 1), sum(1 for v in pc if v > 2),
      sum(1 for v in pc if v == 1),
      sum(1 for s in range(n) if A[s] > Y[s]),
      sum(1 for s in range(n) if A[s] and A[s] == max(lc[s].values()))))

# 0 = kills every rival reading, shows a halved piece beside a whole one of the same
# letter in a counted slice, and cuts one thin and one fat slice.
def grade(b, n, A, raw, P, xy, kk, H, T):
  R = []
  hh = sx = so = one = 0
  off = []
  for i in (0, 1):
    sv, h = tell(b, A, raw, i)
    k, a, o, u, riv = look(b, n, P, xy[i], xy[1 - i], H)
    if k != kk[i]:
      return 3
    R.append(riv)
    off.append(sv - kk[i])
    hh += h
    sx += a
    so += o
    one += u
  bad = lambda j: R[0][j] == kk[0] and R[1][j] == kk[1]
  if not hh or not sx or not so or not one or bad(0) or bad(1):
    return 2
  w = [q - p for p, q in zip([0] + b, b + [T])]
  if (off[0] == off[1] or min(w) > 4 or max(w) - min(w) < 5
      or any(bad(j) for j in range(2, 19))):
    return 1
  return 0

def ren(rows, b):
  out = []
  for row in rows:
    s = ""
    for i, ch in enumerate(row):
      if i in b:
        s += "|"
      s += ch
    out.append(s)
  return out

def chk(clue, s):
  a = clue.split("\n")
  C = [l for l in a[1:] if "." in l]
  R = [l.rstrip() for l in s.split("\n") if "." in l]
  if [l.replace("|", "") for l in R] != C:
    return 0
  S = [l.split("|") for l in R]
  W = [len(g) for g in S[0]]
  n = len(W)
  return int(3 < n < 9 and min(W) > 2 and all([len(g) for g in p] == W for p in S)
       and all(any(h.isalpha() for p in S for h in p[i]) for i in range(n))
       and all(sum(sum(len(re.findall(u[0] + "+", p[i])) for p in S) > 1
             for i in range(n)) == int(u[1])
           for u in (a[0][:2], a[0][2:4])))

def solve(clue):
  a = clue.split("\n")
  xy = (a[0][0], a[0][2])
  kk = (int(a[0][1]), int(a[0][3]))
  rows = [l for l in a[1:] if "." in l]
  H = len(rows)
  T = len(rows[0])
  P = pcs(rows)
  raw, pre = sums(P, T, xy)
  r = random.Random(clue)
  crust = "#" * T
  hold = None
  for it in range(120000):
    if it > 15000 and hold:
      break
    n = r.randint(4, 8)
    if 3 * n > T:
      continue
    b = cutb(r, T, n)
    A = cnt(b, T, pre)
    if A is None or sum(1 for v in A[0] if v > 1) != kk[0] or \
        sum(1 for v in A[1] if v > 1) != kk[1]:
      continue
    g = grade(b, n, A, raw, P, xy, kk, H, T)
    if g > 2:
      continue
    s = "\n".join(ren([crust] + rows + [crust], set(b)))
    if not chk(clue, s):
      continue
    if g == 0:
      return s
    if hold is None or g < hold[0]:
      hold = (g, s)
  return hold[1] if hold else ""
